items.text: The United States and Israel have launched large-scale air strikes across Iran. They said that the goal was to stop Iran from developing nuclear weapons. President Donald Trump described the operation as major combat and warned of possible American casualties . In response, Iran fired missiles at US bases in Bahrain and targeted sites in Qatar and other countries in the region. Several countries reported irockets and drones, and casualties have been reported. Israel declared a state of emergency, closed its airspace, and called up reservists . Explosions were reported in several Iranian cities, including Tehran. During the attacks, Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed, according to announcements by President Trump and Iranian state media. Khamenei had led Iran since 1989, after the death of Ayatollah Khomeini, and had played a key role in Iran’s political and military system since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. The conflict follows weeks of rising tension and negotiations over Iran’s nuclear programme. Many fear the conflict will grow larger. Difficult words: large-scale (very big and involving many people or places), casualty (a person who is killed or injured in an accident or war), reservist (a soldier who is not full-time but can be called to serve in the army). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US and Israel attacked Iran. President Trump said he wanted to stop Iran from becoming a nuclear power and to protect Americans. Iran responded by firing rockets at US military bases in Bahrain and other countries in the region. The countries stopped many rockets in the air, but some hit the ground, killed people and destroyed buildings. Israel declared a state of emergency and closed its airspace . There were explosions Iranian cities. Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei died during the attacks. He led Iran since 1989. The situation follows weeks of protests and talks about Iran’s nuclear programme. Many people worry the conflict could grow larger. Difficult words: state of emergency (a special situation when a government gives itself extra powers because of danger), airspace (the sky above a country), conflict (serious fighting or disagreement, often between countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The United States and Israel attack Iran. President Trump wants to stop Iran from getting nuclear weapons . Iran fires rockets at US bases in the region. Some countries stop the rockets in the air. There are explosions in Iran and Israel. Planes do not fly over these countries now. Iran’s leader, Ali Khamenei, dies during the attacks. He is the leader of Iran since 1989. The fighting starts after weeks of protests and talks about nuclear weapons. Many people are worried that the war will start. Difficult words: nuclear weapon (a very strong bomb), base (a place where soldiers and military thigs stay), explosion (a loud burst which breaks things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A sturgeon farm in Riofrío, southern Spain, produces what it calls the world’s first organic caviar. The product contains only sturgeon eggs and salt, with no additives , and is made entirely in the European Union. The fish are raised in natural spring water and are fed organic vegetables and sustainably sourced fishmeal. According to veterinarian Ignacio Alba Alejandre, the farm doesn’t speed up the sturgeons’ slow growth and allows them to develop naturally. The company produces around two tonnes of caviar each year in three varieties , and exports to countries such as Japan, France, and the UK. The most exclusive type can cost up to 8,000 euros per kilo. In addition, the farm sells about 15 tonnes of sturgeon meat annually. Managers say organic certification guarantees high standards and good flavours. Restaurants in Spain are increasingly adding caviar to their menus, as it has become more affordable. Globally, most caviar now comes from Chinese fish farms. Difficult words: sturgeon (a large fish that lives in rivers or seas and gives eggs used to make caviar), additive (something extra that is added to food to change the taste, colour, or keep it fresh), variety (a different type), exclusive (very special, rare, and often expensive). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In southern Spain, a farm produces organic caviar . The farm makes the caviar only from fish eggs and salt, with no other chemicals. The fish live in clean spring water and eat organic food. The farm does not hurry the fish to grow. It produces about two tonnes of caviar each year and sells it to many countries. The most expensive caviar can cost 8,000 euros per kilo. The company also sells fish meat. Managers say the organic label shows that the product is high quality . Some restaurants now use caviar more often because it is not as expensive as before. Most caviar in the world comes from China. Difficult words: organic (grown or made without artificial chemicals), caviar (fish eggs), label (a piece of information on a product), quality (how good something is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A farm in southern Spain makes organic caviar. Caviar is fish eggs with salt. The fish live in clean water and eat natural food. The farm does not make the fish grow faster. It makes about two tonnes of caviar every year and sells it to many countries. The best caviar can cost 8,000 euros for one kilo. The farm also sells fish meat. The company says that the organic product is very good. Some restaurants now sell more caviar because it is cheaper than before. Most caviar in the world comes from China. Difficult words: organic (when farmers grow plants or animals without chemicals), natural (from nature, not a factory), ton (1,000 kilograms). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US men’s hockey team defeated Canada 2–1 in sudden-death overtime to win its first Olympic gold medal since the famous 1980 “Miracle on Ice.” It was only the second time the United States beat Canada in an Olympic gold medal game. The match was intense, with NHL stars on both sides, many of them normally teammates in the same professional league. Canada outshot the US 42-28, but American goalie Connor Hellebuyck delivered an outstanding performance. After the game was tied 1–1 at the end of regular time, 24-year-old Jack Hughes scored the winning goal in three-on-three overtime. Hughes had earlier lost teeth after he got hit in the face, but he continued playing. This victory also marks the first time both the US men’s and women’s hockey teams are Olympic champions at the same Games. Meanwhile, Norway finished first in the overall medal count. The US placed second. Difficult words: sudden-death (extra time in a game where the first team to score wins immediately), goalie (the player who protects the goal and tries to stop the other team from scoring), victory (a win). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US men’s hockey team beat Canada 2–1 in overtime and won the Olympic gold medal. It is their first gold medal since 1980. The game was very exciting and close. Canada had more shots on goal, but the American goalie played very well. After the score was 1–1 at the end of normal time, Jack Hughes scored the winning goal in overtime. He even lost some teeth earlier in the game, but continued playing. Many of the players are NHL stars and usually play together during the season. This is also the first time that both US men and women won Olympic gold in hockey at the same Games. Norway finished first in total medals, and the United States finished second. Difficult words: overtime (extra time played when there is no winner after the normal time), goalie (the player who stops the puck from going inside the goal), total (the full number or amount). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US men’s hockey team wins the Olympic gold medal. They beat Canada 2–1. The winning goal comes in overtime . The game is fun to watch. Many players are stars in the NHL. They usually play together. Now, they play against each other. The score is 1–1 before overtime. Jack Hughes scores the winning goal. The American goalie plays very well. This is the first gold medal for the US men since 1980. It is also the first time that both US men and women win gold in hockey at the same Olympics. Norway wins the most medals at the Games, and the United States is second. Difficult words: beat (to win against someone), overtime (extra time if nobody wins after normal time), goalie (the player who stops the puck from going inside the goal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At Ichikawa City Zoo near Tokyo, a baby Japanese macaque named Punch has become a popular attraction. When his mother abandoned him shortly after birth, zoo visitors alerted staff, who quickly intervened because baby macaques normally cling to their mothers for strength and security. Keepers tried different substitutes, such as towels and soft toys, before choosing a stuffed orangutan with long hair that Punch could easily hold. They hoped its monkey-like appearance would help him later integrate into the troop . Since then, Punch has rarely been seen without the toy, carrying it everywhere despite its size. Videos of the pair went viral, attracting many visitors. Zookeepers believe extreme summer heat may have caused the mother to abandon him. Although Punch has had some difficulties communicating with other monkeys, staff say he is slowly learning social skills and becoming part of the group. Shoppers have gone crazy for the IKEA plush toy after a video of Punch went viral. Difficult words: alert (to tell someone about a problem or danger), intervene (to step in and help in a situation), troop (a group of monkeys). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A baby monkey named Punch lives at Ichikawa City Zoo in Japan. His mother left him when he was born. Zoo workers helped him because baby monkeys usually stay very close to their mothers. They tried different soft objects to comfort him. Finally, they chose a stuffed orangutan toy because it has long hair and looks a bit like a monkey. Punch now carries the toy everywhere. Many people visit the zoo because videos of Punch became popular online. Also, many people go to IKEA and buy the same toy. The zookeepers think his mother left him because of the very hot weather. Punch is still learning how to communicate with other monkeys, but he is slowly joining the group. Difficult words: stuffed toy (a soft toy filled with cotton or soft material), zookeeper (a person who takes care of animals in a zoo), communicate (to share information or feelings). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A baby monkey named Punch lives in a zoo in Japan. His mother leaves him when he is born. Zoo workers help him. They give him a soft toy to hold. The toy is a stuffed orangutan. Punch likes the toy very much. He carries it everywhere. The toy helps him feel safe. Many people visit the zoo to see Punch and his toy. His videos are very popular online. Many people go and buy the same toy. The zoo workers think that his mother leaves him because it is very hot. Punch is learning to live with other monkeys. One day, he may not need the toy anymore. Difficult words: toy (something to play with), stuffed (filled with soft material), popular (liked by many people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Venezuela has the largest known oil reserves in the world, mainly in the Orinoco Belt. However, most of this oil is extra heavy crude , which is thick, difficult to extract, expensive to refine , and produces very high emissions. Oils from countries such as the United States or Saudi Arabia are lighter, Venezuela’s oil requires special methods like steam or chemical injection to make it flow. It also needs extra upgrading before it can be refined. Even then, it produces products like asphalt and heavy fuel instead of high-demand fuels like gasoline or jet fuel. Also, the extraction process releases large amounts of methane, a powerful greenhouse gas. Poor maintenance of infrastructure has made emissions even worse. Political leaders have shown interest in controlling these reserves, but foreign oil companies are careful because of high costs, environmental impact, and Venezuela’s history of nationalising its oil industry. Future technologies could improve the situation, but this would require bit investment and stability. Difficult words: crude (oil in its natural form, before it is cleaned or processed), refine (a process to make oil usable), asphalt (a black, sticky material used to make roads), nationalising (when a government takes control of a private company or industry). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Venezuela has very large oil reserves , especially in the Orinoco Belt, but most of its oil is heavy and thick. This makes it hard and expensive to take out of the ground and process. It also creates high emissions, including methane , which is very harmful for the planet. Lighter oils from other countries are easier to extract and give better products like gasoline. Venezuela’s oil often becomes asphalt or heavy fuel, which are not so good. The country’s oil industry also has many problems, such as broken equipment and poor maintenance. In the past, foreign oil companies had to leave, so investors are careful. Some future technologies could make the oil easier to use, but this would need a lot of money and time. Difficult words: reserve (a supply of something kept for future use), methane (a strong greenhouse gas that can harm the climate), extract (to take something out from the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Venezuela has a lot of oil under the ground. It has one of the biggest oil reserves in the world. But most of this oil is very thick and heavy. It is hard and expensive to get it out. It also makes a lot of pollution . This oil does not make much gasoline. It mostly makes asphalt and heavy fuel. These products are not so good. Venezuela’s oil industry also has problems. Some machines are old and broken. In the past, the government sends foreign oil companies away, so companies are careful now. In the future, new technology could help. But this will need time and money. Difficult words: reserve (a supply of something what you want to use in the future), pollution (dirty substances in the air, water, or land), foreign (from another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

France and Germany disagree about a new fighter jet that is still under development. France wants the aircraft to carry nuclear weapons and operate from an aircraft carrier, because it uses both. Germany doesn’t have nuclear arms or carriers, so it sees these demands as unnecessary. This difference has created tension inside the joint European project, which began in 2017 as part of a future combat air system planned for 2040. The project is not only about a jet. It also includes software, unmanned aircraft, and a system that connects different air units. However, the fighter jet is a central part, and public doubt from German leaders has raised concern. Competition between major aerospace companies has made the situation even more difficult, especially over who should lead and how costs should be shared. Europe wants to reduce dependence on the United States for defense equipment. Some experts say the wider program could continue even if the countries develop separate jets Difficult words: demand (to strongly ask for something), tension (a feeling of stress or conflict between people or groups), unmanned (without a person inside). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

France and Germany don’t agree about a new fighter jet. France wants the plane to carry nuclear weapons and work from an aircraft carrier. Germany doesn’t have these weapons or ships, so it doesn’t need this. The two countries started this project together in 2017 as part of a future air defense system . The project also includes software and aircraft without a pilot, not only a jet. But the jet is very important. German leaders spoke openly about problems with this deal. Big companies in both countries also compete for control and money. Europe wants to depend less on the United States for military planes. This disagreement shows that it is sometimes hard to work together. Experts say the program might continue even if the countries build different jets. Difficult words: air defense system (planes, weapons, and technology that keep a country safe from attacks in the air), compete (to try to win or be better than someone else), disagreement (a situation where people have different opinions). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

France and Germany plan a new fighter plane. But they do not agree . France wants the plane to carry nuclear weapons and work from a big ship for planes. Germany does not have these weapons or ships, so it does not need this. The two countries start the project together in 2017. The plan is about a new plane, computer systems, and small planes without pilots. The plane is very important for the plan. Leaders in Germany now speak about the problems. Europe wants to make its own fighter planes and not depend on the United States. This problem shows that working together is not easy. The project may continue, but it is not clear what will happen. Difficult words: agree (to think the same), nuclear weapon (a very strong bomb), depend (to need someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tipo Cafe in Livigno is offering special cappuccinos with the Milano Cortina 2026 logo and mascots , located very close to the slopes where snowboarding and freestyle skiing events happen. The cafe wants to give visitors a fun and unique experience while celebrating the Olympic Games. Italy uses this event to show its culture, including food and drinks, as part of the Olympic spirit. The cafe owner explained that a cappuccino is part of what Italy does best, alongside pizza and other foods. The idea is to combine the excitement of the Olympics with a warm, enjoyable drink in the mountains. Visitors can enjoy hot drinks that give energy and make them feel happy while watching the sports. Many people appreciate this small gesture . They see it as a fun way to connect with the games and the atmosphere around Livigno. A customer said they ordered a cappuccino and received a lovely surprise, making the Olympic experience even more memorable. Difficult words: mascot (a character that represents something), unique (special or very unusual), gesture (action that shows a thought or feeling). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Tipo Cafe in Livigno makes cappuccinos with the Milano Cortina 2026 logo and mascots . The cafe is near the slopes where snowboarding and freestyle skiing events happen. The owner wants visitors to have a special and fun experience while celebrating the Olympic Games. They said a cappuccino is part of Italy’s best food and drinks, together with pizza and other foods. The idea is to mix the Olympic spirit with a warm drink in the mountains. Hot drinks can give energy and make people happy while they watch sports. Many visitors like this small idea and enjoy the games. One customer said they ordered a cappuccino and got a lovely surprise. Difficult words: mascot (a character that represents something), slope (a hill or mountain for skiing and snowboarding), spirit (the feeling or mood of an event or group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tipo Cafe in Livigno gives cappuccinos with the Milano Cortina 2026 picture and mascots . The cafe is near the mountains where people ski and snowboard. The owner wants people to have fun and enjoy the Olympic Games. They said that cappuccino is one of Italy’s best drinks, along with pizza and other foods. The plan is to give people a warm drink and a happy feeling in the mountains. The drinks give energy while people watch the sports. Many people like this idea. One visitor said that they order a cappuccino and get a nice surprise . Difficult words: mascot (a character or animal which represents a team or event), owner (the person who has a business), surprise (something you do not know will happen, and it makes you happy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A study has found that several sunscreen chemicals are absorbed into the bloodstream even after a single use. Researchers tested the absorption of six active ingredients found in four commercially available sunscreen products. Participants applied sunscreen to 75% of their bodies over four days, and scientists found that all six ingredients were absorbed into the bloodstream, and they remained in participants’ bodies for days. They also found that the concentration levels exceeded safety limits. Despite these findings, scientists still recommend to continue to use sunscreens for their recognized public health benefits. Experts say that more research is needed to understand the chemicals’ absorption into the body and what effects that absorption may have. Difficult words: absorb (take in), bloodstream (the blood circulating through the body), exceed (to go past an allowed limit). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists tested four sunscreen products and their ingredients . Participants of the study applied sunscreen on their bodies for four days. Scientists found out that six chemicals got into the participants’ blood, and they stayed there for several days. The amount of these chemicals were higher than the safe limits; however, it is important to use sunscreens. They have health benefits because they protect the skin from dangerous sunburns. Scientists must do more research to understand how chemicals get into the body and what effects they can have. It is necessary to make rules for sunscreen products and to check the safety of the chemicals that they contain. Difficult words: sunscreen (a cream that protects the skin from the sun), ingredient (a part of a product), participant (a person who takes part in an activity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People use sunscreens to protect their skin from the sun. There is a new study. It says that some chemicals in sunscreens get into people’s blood. Scientists test four different sunscreens and six chemicals. They find that all six chemicals get into the body. They do not know what these chemicals do to people. It is worrying. Scientists must do more research to understand how chemicals get into the body. Some chemicals in sunscreens can be dangerous. However, scientists say that the health benefits of sunscreens are bigger than the risks. Officials must control sunscreens more and check the chemicals in them. Difficult words: sunscreen (a cream that stops the sun from burning the skin), protect (to keep safe), chemical (a thing that scientists work with that people use to make other things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Our addiction to digital devices, despite knowing they are not always good for us, can be explained by the role of dopamine, a neurotransmitter in our brain. Dopamine is responsible for pleasure, motivation, and reward. When we engage in activities like scrolling on social media, our brain releases dopamine, making us feel good and encouraging us to do it again. However, over time, our brain adapts and releases less dopamine. This can create a cycle where we need to constantly seek new, rewarding experiences, which leads to an imbalance of dopamine in our brains. This imbalance may affect our attention span, making it harder to focus on tasks. Digital media overstimulate our brain, and as a result, we develop a tolerance, just like in addiction. The constant search for new dopamine hits can result in a feeling of stress and anxiety, leaving us less satisfied with everyday activities. Difficult words: neurotransmitter (a chemical in the brain that transmits signals), imbalance (a lack of balance), overstimulate (to excite too much). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People often get hooked on their phones and devices even when they know it is bad for them. This happens because of a chemical in our brain called dopamine. Dopamine makes us feel pleasure, motivation, and reward. When we scroll through social media, our brain releases dopamine, which makes us want to do it more. But if we keep doing this, our brain gets used to it and starts releasing less dopamine. This can cause problems like not being able to focus on other things. The more we use our devices, the more we need new things to feel the same pleasure, which can lead to a feeling of stress. This makes it harder to enjoy real-life activities and may cause anxiety . Difficult words: hooked (enjoying something so much that you are not able to stop), release (to let go), anxiety (a feeling of worry or nervousness). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

We often use our phones too much. But we know that it is bad for us. This happens because of a chemical in our brain called dopamine. Dopamine makes us feel happy and motivated . When we scroll on our phones, our brain gives us dopamine. It makes us want to do it again. But over time, our brain gets used to it. The brain gives us less dopamine. This can make it hard to focus and enjoy other activities. Too much time on devices can also make us feel stressed and anxious . Difficult words: motivated (feeling that you want to do something), to focus (to look at, listen to, or think about only one thing), anxious (feeling nervous or worried). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hungary and Slovakia have stopped sending diesel to Ukraine because oil deliveries through the Druzhba pipeline were damaged. Both countries say Ukraine hasn’t fixed the pipeline and call this a political choice. Hungary also said Ukraine tried to use energy as a tool to influence politics. The pipeline was damaged by a Russian air strike, which stopped oil transfers at the end of January. Officials from both countries said they have enough fuel for their own people but want to keep diesel inside their borders. Slovakia has also used emergency oil reserves to secure its domestic supply. Hungary and Slovakia asked the European Commission to allow Russian oil to move through Croatia, but Croatia said it could break US sanctions. The European Commission said that both countries have enough energy and their safety is not at risk. Ukraine is facing serious energy problems because Russian attacks damaged its infrastructure during winter, and the diesel halt makes the situation worse. Difficult words: pipeline (a long tube that moves oil or gas from one place to another), reserve (extra supply kept for future use), halt (to stop something from moving or happening). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hungary and Slovakia stopped sending diesel to Ukraine because the Druzhba pipeline was broken. They said Ukraine didn’t fix it, and this is a political decision. Hungary said Ukraine tried to use oil to affect politics. The Russian attack caused the damage at the end of January. Both countries said they have enough fuel for their people and want to keep diesel at home. Slovakia also used oil from emergency storage . Hungary and Slovakia asked the European Commission to move Russian oil through Croatia, but Croatia said it may break US rules. The Commission said energy safety is not a problem. Ukraine has serious energy problems because Russian attacks broke its systems during winter, and stopping diesel makes it worse. Difficult words: diesel (fuel used in cars, trucks, or machines), pipeline (a long tube that moves oil or gas from one place to another), emergency storage (a place where things are stored for urgent situations). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hungary and Slovakia do not send diesel to Ukraine now. The oil pipe is broken because of a Russian attack. Both countries say that Ukraine does not fix the pipe. They keep diesel for their own people. Slovakia uses oil from storage to help people. Hungary and Slovakia want to move Russian oil through Croatia, but Croatia says no. The European Commission says both countries have enough oil. Ukraine has big problems with energy. Russian attacks break its systems. Stopping diesel makes it harder for people there. Difficult words: diesel (fuel which people use in cars, trucks, or machines), pipe (a tube which carries water, gas, or oil from one place to another), storage (a place where you keep things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South Korea’s former president, Yoon Suk Yeol, has received a life sentence after a court found him guilty of insurrection . Judges said he led an illegal action when he declared martial law in December 2024. They said he sent soldiers to the National Assembly in an attempt to block its work and take control of the country’s political system. The court also punished other officials, including the former defence minister and the former police chief. Prosecutors had asked for the death penalty , but the judge decided that life in prison was a strong enough sentence. Yoon has said he is innocent and plans to appeal the decision. The case caused big political changes across the country. Large protests took place both for and against Yoon. This trial is important because it shows how the law deals with a leader accused of abuse of power. Difficult words: life sentence (a punishment where a person stays in prison for the rest of their life), insurrection (a violent action to fight against the government and try to take power), martial law (a time when the army controls a country instead of normal government leaders), death penalty (a legal punishment where the state kills a person for a very serious crime). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A court in South Korea gave former president Yoon Suk Yeol a life sentence, which means that he will spend the rest of his life in prison. The court says he led an insurrection in 2024. Judges say he sent soldiers to the National Assembly to stop its work. They believe he tried to take control of the country. The court also gave prison sentences to other top officials, including the former defence minister . Yoon says he did nothing wrong and plans to appeal . Many people protest outside the court. Some support him, but others celebrate the decision. The case brings political changes and a strong public reaction. Difficult words: insurrection (a fight against the government), defence minister (the government leader who controls the army), appeal (to ask a higher court to change a legal decision). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A court in South Korea gives former president Yoon Suk Yeol life in prison . The court says that he wants to change the political system in the country in 2024. He sends soldiers to stop the judges . He wants to take power over the country. The court also gives prison time to other leaders, like a minister and the boss of the police. Yoon says he does nothing wrong. He wants to go to court again. Many people stand outside the court. Some feel angry, and some feel happy. The case brings political changes in the country. Difficult words: former (the one from the past), prison (a place where you stay if you do something bad), judge (a person in a court who says what is right).

Singapore has a very good public transport system, but one advocate says even the best systems have blind spots . To help people find their way, he has been putting up his own signs. The signs look official, but they are done by Veric, a young man who calls himself a gorilla wayfinder. He started by installing signs at a university after missing buses late at night. He then expanded to public spaces and has completed at least ten projects. Veric studies transit maps and designs signs that show complete bus routes and transfer points. He often works at night to avoid public attention . The man’s goal is to make travel easier and clearer for commuters. He says a good design is simple and easy to use, so people don’t have to think about it. Before this, he complained online about poor signage , but now he takes action and hopes his work inspires others to improve their community. Difficult words: advocate (someone who supports an idea), blind spot (a place you cannot see or notice easily), attention (the act of watching or focusing on something), signage (signs in an area that give information or directions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Singapore has a very good public transport system, but some places are still hard to find. A young man named Veric puts up signs to help people. His signs look official, but he makes them himself. He started at a university because the bus stops had no signs. Now he also works in public areas, and he did many projects. Veric works at night so that he doesn’t meet many people. He studies maps to make his signs clear. His signs show the full bus route and where to change buses. Veric wants travel to be easy for everyone. Before this, he complained online about bad signs. But nothing changed, so he decided to change things himself. He hopes others will also try to make the city better. Difficult words: sign (a board or mark that shows information or directions), route (the way or path you follow to go somewhere), complain (to say you are not happy about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Singapore has a very good bus and train system . But some places are hard to find. A young man named Veric puts up signs to help people. The signs look like official signs, but he makes them. Veric starts at a university because the bus stops have no signs. Now he also works in other areas . He does many signs. Veric works at night and looks at maps to make his signs clear. He wants travel to be easy. Before this, he writes about bad signs online. Nothing changes. He starts to change things himself. He thinks that other people will help make the city better. Difficult words: system (parts which work together), sign (a board or label with information), area (a part of a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Mark Zuckerberg, the head of Meta, spoke in court during an important trial about the impact of social media on young people. A 20-year-old woman says she began to use Instagram and YouTube at a very young age and later faced addiction, depression, and suicidal thoughts. She believes these platforms caused serious harm in her life. Her lawyer showed company emails that talked about a growing number of users and time spent on the apps. The lawyer also pointed to a company email about age limits. Meta says children under 13 cannot join, but the email raised concern that this rule didn’t always work. Zuckerberg said he regrets that the company didn’t act faster. He also said the company tried to improve its rules over time. Many families say social media can hurt children. Some parents say they want justice and change. The result of this trial may affect future law and the way social media companies work. Difficult words: suicidal (wanting to kill yourself), concern (a worry about something), justice (a fair result). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Mark Zuckerberg goes to court in an important case about social media and young people. A 20-year-old woman says she started to use Instagram and YouTube when she was very young. She says she later felt addicted and depressed. She believes the apps hurt her mental health. Her lawyer shows emails from the company. In the email, Meta bosses spoke about the growing number of users and time on the apps. The lawyer also talked about age limits . Meta said children under 13 couldn’t join the apps, but emails showed problems with this rule. Zuckerberg said he was sorry that the company didn’t act faster. He says the company tries to make its apps safer. Many parents want a change. They want social media companies to be responsible. This case may affect future rules. Difficult words: addicted (not able to stop doing or using something), age limit (the youngest or oldest age allowed), act (to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Year of the Horse begins in 2026, and people born in this year are believed to be energetic, social, stubborn , and hardworking. Horses in Chinese culture represent success, ambition , and passion. This year is a fire-horse year, meaning the element fire influences it. In Chinese philosophy, five elements interact to support or restrain each other, and each year carries its own element. Horses are important in history, literature, and legends. Ancient stories describe powerful horses carrying heroes and emperors, and famous works like Journey to the West feature horses as symbols of bravery and perseverance . Horses also changed wars, transport, and communication, and helped humans develop. Today, horses appear in logos for brands, cars, and banks. Younger Chinese people now use the horse spirit to describe hard work and long hours. Lunar New Year is celebrated in many Asian countries and beyond, withamily gatherings, traditional food, and festivals. Difficult words: stubborn (not willing to change your mind or behavior), ambition (a strong wish to achieve something important), restrain (to hold back or control something), perseverance (the ability to keep going even when it is difficult). In Nigeria, scorpion venom farming is emerging as a lucrative business, with farms aiming to sell venom to the global market. Nepal celebrated Shivaratri in Kathmandu as large crowds gathered at Pashupatinath Temple to honor the god Shiva. Tens of thousands of people waited in long lines to pray, sing, and dance. However, police show rare tolerance during this festival because of Shiva’s traditional link to cannabis. Some groups have tried to change the law, but these efforts haven’t moved forward. For this one day, tradition becomes more important than strict control, and the country allows limited cannabis use as part of the religious celebration. Difficult words: ritual (actions done in a special way for a ceremony or tradition), marijuana (a plant people sometimes smoke for its mind-changing effects), devotee (a person who strongly supports or takes part in a religion or activity).
